# Stored SVG images go through one helper

## Applies when

Showing an SVG image that a user stored — a flow image (`flow.image`), the copy a pipeline keeps of it, or
anything else saved as SVG markup — anywhere in this app.

**Not this if**: the SVG is generated by the app itself at runtime (a BPMN viewer's own canvas, chart
libraries). Those are not user-written markup. The BPMN preview images of process models, deployments and
smart-service designs are already shown as data URLs and are outside this rule.

## Rule

Stored SVG markup never reaches the page through `bypassSecurityTrustHtml`. It goes through
`src/app/core/svg-image.ts`:

- `parseSvgImage(markup)` parses it as XML and returns `null` unless it is well-formed with an `svg` root.
  A page shows no image for `null`.
- `svgImageDataUrl(svg)` for display only: bind the result to `<img [src]>`. An image document runs no
  script and fires no handler. Angular's URL sanitizer accepts the `data:` URL, no bypass is needed.
- `svgImageMarkup(svg)` only where the page needs the SVG as live DOM, for clicks on operators: bind it to
  `[innerHtml]`. It rebuilds the tree from an allowlist of SVG elements and drops every `on*` attribute,
  every `href` not starting with `#`, and CSS functions other than transforms and colours.

Edits such as highlighting an operator happen on the parsed element before either call.

| Site | Path |
|---|---|
| flow list preview (`data/flow-repo`) | `<img>` |
| pipeline details | `<img>` |
| flow deploy, new export, smart-service task dialog | allowlist markup, they hit-test live nodes |

## What changes for an image

- The flow designer writes a lower-case `viewbox`, which XML does not know; the helper writes `viewBox` on
  the root.
- An `<img>` cannot load the page's web fonts. The helper names Roboto, which renders only where it is
  installed locally, otherwise a sans-serif fallback.
- Ids nothing in the image refers to are dropped.
